net-03.title: The catch is sorted
net-03.alt: Three fishermen sort fish beside baskets on the shore, with a wooden boat behind them.
net-03.caption: The gathered catch is examined on the shore, with some fish placed in baskets and others set apart. Jesus uses this separation to teach about judgment at the end of the world. He identifies angels as the agents of that final division; the comparison does not appoint readers to determine their neighbors' ultimate worth.

pearl-02.title: One pearl of great worth
pearl-02.alt: A seated merchant examines a single pearl between his fingers while a seller holds an empty folded cloth.
pearl-02.caption: One pearl holds the merchant's attention. Jesus describes the recognition of something so valuable that the merchant is willing to sell all he has to obtain it. The image illustrates that moment of recognition before the purchase, inviting reflection on how we respond to the kingdom's surpassing worth.

lost-sheep-03.title: Rejoicing with neighbors
lost-sheep-03.alt: A shepherd welcomes three neighbors at his doorway while a white-faced cream-colored sheep stands beside him.
lost-sheep-03.caption: The shepherd calls others to share his joy over the sheep he has found. Luke's account carries the recovery beyond a private moment into rejoicing with friends and neighbors, then connects that joy with repentance. The welcome invites us to receive another person's return with gladness.
